The National Coordinator of the All Progressives Grand Alliance Media Warriors Forum, Chinedu Obigwe, has warned Anambra voters against rejecting President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election. This came following Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s endorsement of the President’s re-election bid. Obigwe described voting for Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, as a wasted vote, warning that those who choose to support him should be prepared for the consequences of an electoral defeat. He urged voters in the state and the wider South-East to support Tinubu’s second-term ambition, arguing that doing so would enable Anambra to negotiate for greater development support from the Federal Government. Obigwe made the remarks in a statement issued in Awka on Wednesday, where he advised voters to put aside what he described as emotional sentiments and support Tinubu’s re-election. The statement read, “Anybody in Anambra joking with Governor Soludo’s advice with regard to the forthcoming 2027 general election is doing so to the detriment of our state and also to his or her own peril. “If you already know that Peter Obi will not win the 2027 general election and still decide to vote for him so that you will fail the election with him, you should as well get ready to face the consequence of failure. In politics, you bargain with your votes, according to Governor Chukwuma Soludo. Voting massively for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu 2nd term re election is the best thing for Anambra voters to do. Umunnem ndi Anambra, let’s follow who know road.” Soludo has publicly backed Tinubu’s bid for a second term ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The governor has argued that supporting the President could strengthen the South-East’s relationship with the Federal Government and improve the region’s prospects of securing development projects. The All Progressives Grand Alliance has also adopted Tinubu as its preferred presidential candidate for the 2027 election and announced that it would not field its own candidate. At the launch of the party’s 2027 campaign in Awka on November 6, Soludo said APGA was targeting at least 50 per cent of Anambra’s votes for the President. The governor’s position has drawn attention because Anambra gave Tinubu fewer than 5,000 votes in the 2023 presidential election, while Peter Obi, who contested on the Labour Party platform at the time, secured 584,621 votes in the state.
